title: Can You Guess How Your Fridge Gets Cold?
summary: A fridge does not make cold. It moves heat from inside to the outside, using a liquid that boils and gets squeezed again and again.

beats.text: Does your fridge add cold, move heat out, or freeze the air? Pause and guess!

visual.text: How does a fridge get cold?

beats.text: Cold is not a thing you can add. It just means less heat.
Time's up. What does a fridge really do?
beats.reveal: It moves heat out! Warmth travels from inside the fridge to the coils at the back.

visual.question: What does a fridge really do?

beats.text: A special liquid in the pipes soaks up heat and turns to gas. A pump squeezes it, and the back coils let the heat go.
That is why the back of a fridge feels warm.
Bonus fact: an open door warms your room, not cools it.

visual.text: An open fridge warms a room: it pumps heat out the back, plus motor heat.
